source.title_on_document: Enhancing heritage-oriented design learning through a value-sensitive approach to generative AI in higher education aesthetic pedagogy

supplement.where: Supplementary Information at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-71408-2 (p. 12, Additional information); code, LoRA weights and inference script in the Zenodo repository, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20688143 (p. 10, Data availability)
supplement.holds: The external supplementary file is described as the R script used to generate all inferential statistics; its contents were not read here (p. 10, Data availability; p. 12, Additional information). Appendix A is included in this PDF on p. 10 and describes the minimal reproducible inference workflow, including hardware, environment setup, model-weight integration, and pipeline execution. Statistics also occur outside the main tables: computational ablation estimates and confidence intervals on p. 4, expert-rating ICCs on p. 5, and simple-main-effect mean differences, standard errors, and confidence intervals on p. 6.

paper_design_summary: A 12-week quasi-experiment assigned intact class sections of 118 second-year design students in a Chinese university industrial and fashion design program to traditional design methods (n = 59) or a custom Stable Diffusion v1.5 pipeline with heritage-specific LoRA fine-tuning and ControlNet (n = 59); the number of class sections and random allocation are not stated (p. 3, Methodology). Students translated Xiang Embroidery and Changsha Kiln ceramics into modern designs, with three blinded experts scoring final artifacts on cultural authenticity, design innovation, and technical feasibility from 1 to 100, alongside 7-point self-report scales administered at Weeks 1 and 12 (pp. 4-5, Methodology). A separate model-only ablation compared LoRA networks trained on uncorrected versus RestoreFormer++-calibrated archaeological images using 500 generated outputs per model and FID and CLIP scores (p. 4, Dataset provenance, curation, and annotation protocol).

assignment.what_was_assigned: Intact class sections were assigned to the control group (traditional design methods) or the experimental group (VSD-guided generative AI pipeline); the paper does not say how the sections were allocated.
assignment.quote: To maintain ecological validity within the university structure, intact class sections were assigned to either the Control Group (n = 59) or the Experimental Group (n = 59), which strictly justifies the quasi-experimental design.

arms.name: Control Group
arms.description: Conventional aesthetic education curriculum: manual sketching, traditional computer-aided design software (Adobe Illustrator, Rhino), and physical prototyping to translate Xiang Embroidery and Changsha Kiln elements into modern commercial designs (p. 3).

arms.name: Experimental Group
arms.description: Localized Stable Diffusion v1.5 deployment with custom LoRA models (trained via Kohya_ss on curated Xiang Embroidery and Changsha Kiln datasets) and ControlNet spatial conditioning, used iteratively from ideation to final high-fidelity rendering (pp. 3 to 4).

participants.exclusions: Before the sample was formed, individuals with prior systematic training in diffusion models or incomplete attendance records were removed (p. 3); the number removed is not stated. Table 2 ANOVA degrees of freedom (1, 116) are consistent with 118 analyzed.
participants.who: Second-year undergraduate design students in a university industrial and fashion design program (68 females, 50 males; mean age 20.4, SD 1.1)
participants.quote: The final sample consisted of 118 participants (68 females, 50 males; mean age = 20.4, SD = 1.1).

ai_tool.name_model: Stable Diffusion v1.5 with custom Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) models fine-tuned via Kohya_ss on curated Xiang Embroidery (1,500 images) and Changsha Kiln (2,000 images) datasets, plus ControlNet (Canny edge and depth) spatial conditioning; datasets tagged with Qwen-VL
ai_tool.how_used: Students in the experimental group used the pipeline throughout the 12-week course to iteratively develop design concepts from ideation to final high-fidelity rendering, inputting structural sketches of modern products and prompts; the pipeline applied heritage textures under ControlNet geometry constraints (p. 4).

task.description: Translate two regional heritages (Xiang Embroidery, Changsha Kiln ceramics) into modern commercial design artifacts; each student submitted a final design portfolio containing their translated heritage artifact at the end of the course (p. 5).

outcomes.name: Expert evaluation of final design artifact: Design Innovation
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Blinded panel of three independent experts (one intangible cultural heritage inheritor, one senior industrial designer, one academic design theorist) scored each final artifact on a 1 to 100 rubric; ICC for Design Innovation = 0.93 (p. 5). Compared by independent samples t-test (p. 8, Table 3).

contrasts.reported: Control Group Mean (SD) 68.9 (9.6) vs Experimental Group Mean (SD) 87.9 (6.6); t-value 12.57, p < 0.001

outcomes.name: Expert evaluation of final design artifact: Cultural Authenticity
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same three-expert blinded panel, 1 to 100 rubric; cultural authenticity of the translated heritage motifs; ICC = 0.89 (p. 5). Independent samples t-test (p. 8, Table 3).

contrasts.reported: Control Group Mean (SD) 72.4 (8.2) vs Experimental Group Mean (SD) 86.7 (6.4); t-value 10.61, p < 0.001

outcomes.name: Expert evaluation of final design artifact: Technical Feasibility
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same three-expert blinded panel, 1 to 100 rubric; ICC = 0.84 (p. 5). Independent samples t-test (p. 8, Table 3).

contrasts.reported: Control Group Mean (SD) 76.5 (7.9) vs Experimental Group Mean (SD) 81.4 (8.0); t-value 3.34, p-value 0.001

assignment.what_was_assigned: No people were assigned. Identical LoRA networks were trained under the same hyperparameters on uncorrected archaeological images or on images calibrated by RestoreFormer++; the random sampling described concerns generated outputs, not assignment of people.
assignment.quote: We trained two identical Low-Rank Adaptation networks under the same hyperparameters: a baseline model trained on the uncorrected archaeological images, and an experimental model trained on the dataset calibrated by RestoreFormer++.
assignment.locator: p. 4, Dataset provenance, curation, and annotation protocol, computational ablation paragraph

arms.name: LoRA trained on uncorrected archaeological images
arms.description: Baseline LoRA network trained on uncorrected archaeological images; a random sample of 500 generated outputs was evaluated (p. 4, computational ablation paragraph).

arms.name: LoRA trained on RestoreFormer++-calibrated images
arms.description: Otherwise identical LoRA network trained on archaeological images calibrated by RestoreFormer++, using the same hyperparameters; a random sample of 500 generated outputs was evaluated (p. 4, computational ablation paragraph).

participants.exclusions: No human participant exclusions apply to this computational ablation; exclusions from the generated-output evaluation sample are not stated.
participants.who: No human participants in the ablation. The reported sample is 500 generated outputs from each model, not people.
participants.quote: Evaluating a random sample of 500 generative outputs from each, the ablation revealed a substantial performance divergence.
participants.locator: p. 4, Dataset provenance, curation, and annotation protocol, computational ablation paragraph

ai_tool.name_model: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) networks, with versus without RestoreFormer++ calibration of the archaeological training images
ai_tool.how_used: The authors trained identical networks under the same hyperparameters and evaluated random samples of generated outputs to assess whether preprocessing suppressed historical degradation artifacts (p. 4, computational ablation paragraph).

task.description: Generate images from models trained on archaeological imagery and compare their image fidelity and semantic alignment; no human creative task was assigned in this ablation (p. 4, computational ablation paragraph).

outcomes.name: Fréchet Inception Distance (FID)
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Model-output fidelity assessed by FID on a random sample of 500 generated outputs from each model. The reported result is a set-level model comparison; the number of independent evaluation sets or replicates and the confidence-interval method are not stated, so n_units is null. This is not an across-person diversity measure (p. 4, computational ablation paragraph).

contrasts.control_arm: LoRA trained on uncorrected archaeological images
contrasts.reported: Restored model FID score reduced by approximately 16.4, 95% CI: [-18.20, -14.60], compared to the baseline.
contrasts.locator: p. 4, Dataset provenance, curation, and annotation protocol, computational ablation paragraph

outcomes.name: CLIP semantic alignment score
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: CLIP semantic alignment of generated outputs. n_units = 500 is the explicitly reported random output sample per model, not a pooled total or a people count. The CLIP model version, aggregation procedure, and confidence-interval method are not stated (p. 4, computational ablation paragraph).

contrasts.control_arm: LoRA trained on uncorrected archaeological images
contrasts.reported: Restored model CLIP semantic alignment score increased by 0.07, 95% CI: [0.064, 0.076], compared to the baseline.
contrasts.locator: p. 4, Dataset provenance, curation, and annotation protocol, computational ablation paragraph

eligibility.reason: Criterion 1 not met: the paper assigns intact class sections to the control or experimental group, calls the people study quasi-experimental, and does not state random allocation or the number of class sections (p. 3, Methodology). Criterion 2 met for S1: 118 students analyzed, 59 per group (p. 3, Methodology). Criterion 3 met for S1: a blinded three-expert panel scored final design artifacts on design innovation, cultural authenticity, and technical feasibility (p. 5, artifact evaluation paragraph; p. 8, Table 3). The 7-point self-report psychometric outcomes do not establish output-scored creativity (p. 4, psychometric assessment paragraph; p. 6, Tables 1-2). S1 remains observational context because people were compared with and without AI under a nonrandomized design. S2 is a model-only computational ablation: its 500 generated outputs per model are not people and do not establish randomized AI assistance to people (p. 4, computational ablation paragraph). It does not qualify for the core dataset or independently supply one of the permitted context classes.

one_line_finding: In a 12-week quasi-experiment with 118 Chinese design students in intact class sections, the group using a heritage-tuned Stable Diffusion/LoRA/ControlNet pipeline received higher blinded expert scores on final design artifacts than the traditional-methods group: Design Innovation 87.9 (SD 6.6) vs 68.9 (SD 9.6), t = 12.57, p < 0.001; Cultural Authenticity 86.7 (6.4) vs 72.4 (8.2), t = 10.61; Technical Feasibility 81.4 (8.0) vs 76.5 (7.9), t = 3.34, p = 0.001 (p. 8, Table 3).
notes: Internal discrepancy on p. 8: Figure 2 annotates Design Innovation with Control 68.9/9.5 and Experimental 88.2/7.1, whereas Table 3 gives means (SDs) of 68.9 (9.6) and 87.9 (6.6). For Cultural Authenticity, Figure 2 annotates Control 72.4/8.1 and Experimental 86.7/6.3, versus Table 3 values 72.4 (8.2) and 86.7 (6.4). For Technical Feasibility, the Figure 2 Control annotation is 76.5/7.8, versus 76.5 (7.9) in Table 3. The S1 reported statistics and one-line finding retain the correctly transcribed Table 3 values; these conflicting figure annotations remain unresolved. The code repository address is transcribed from the article, with no verification of its current accessibility or contents. No public participant-data URL is stated, and the raw image dataset is explicitly unavailable for public distribution (p. 10, Data availability).

applied.old: A 12-week quasi-experiment in a university industrial and fashion design program in Hunan, China, with 118 second-year design students.
